summary: The shared work board was tidied: finished claims were removed and one builder's in-flight pages were listed.

A new house rule now applies to every page: show the least a person needs first (the answer, a few rows, one action) and keep detail one quiet tap away. The owner's own words are saved so every future session follows them.
points: Retirement pages are the first to be reshaped under the rule.

summary: A safety check that runs before changes reach the phone link was failing because it looked for old wording. The pages were right, so the check now looks for "Not connected to your computer", the words people really see.
points: The check passes with no request sent to the site's computer link.
numbers: 2 pages (Audit and Backups) were being flagged

summary: One builder posted on the work board that it is ready for the next review round.

On Our guesses, the page no longer snaps back when you swipe down, so "Continue your plan" can be reached after you keep every row. The "Matters less" section also stays open while you keep rows inside it, instead of folding shut each time.
points: Scrolling to the bottom now works after the last row is kept.
Opening "Matters less" stays open for that visit.

summary: The phone link now opens even on a weak connection. It keeps the last whole version of the app on the phone and opens from it if the site does not answer in 4 seconds, and it never mixes two versions. An unchanged site now opens with 1 request instead of about 570.
points: "Opening your plan..." says it is still trying after 8 seconds and reloads once after 15 seconds of nothing.
With no computer set up, the app asks the site for nothing.
A saved copy is dropped after two bad opens, or 30 days.
The safety hooks are installed once per copy of the project.
numbers: 1 request instead of about 570 on an unchanged site

summary: The monthly "left over" figure is now stated in plainer words and in the right amount: a typed leftover is rounded to the nearest $2 and called "about", and a negative month reads "checking going down $X a month". A rental's rent now counts after its running costs and loan on every page, and the financial statements add up to the same month.
points: With nothing coming in, the page asks for income first.
Expenses offers "My spending is right" or "What's left over is right".
Retyping the retirement figure never makes the answer worse and keeps your loans.
A working year's tax is paid from that year's pay, not from savings.
The careful money-lasts figure now settles at 9 of 10 paths.
numbers: 14 households with only debts are now asked for savings
Retirement answer for the test household stays 12,810

summary: An independent reviewer closed one finding on Our guesses and posted two new ones (a stuck scroll and a section that re-folds).

points: The blank space was 971 px tall on a 390 px phone and 555 px on a 320 px phone; it now settles at the page's normal 121 px.
numbers: 971 px of blank reduced to 121 px

summary: On Our guesses, a resting thumb no longer gets a button dropped under it. Rows only let go of their space after your own next scroll, so nothing slides into the place you were about to tap.
points: The jump under a resting thumb was 679 px before and is 0 now.

points: Held space lets go only when it will not move what you are about to tap.

The home-value guess no longer jumps where one survey group takes over.
Home insurance has a floor of $350 or 2.55% of the value, whichever is less.
No figure you typed moves; four "usually spend" guesses do.
numbers: 4 guess-only figures moved, 0 typed figures moved
